title: Chatbots might be coming to Apple’s HomeView
summary: iOS 27.3 beta code suggests chatbots coming to Apple HomeView
detailed: Code in the iOS 27.3 beta indicates Apple is adding a 'Conversational Apps' category, suggesting potential chatbot support for its HomeView smart home hub.
The beta includes support for bidirectional audio routing and session management, though they are not fully wired up.
Apple added anti-spoofing protection requiring user authentication with an iPhone after three failed attempts, alongside a lockout system scaling from one to eight hours.
Neither feature has been officially announced by Apple, and availability dates are unconfirmed.
This matters because it signals potential integration of conversational AI assistants into Apple's smart home hardware ecosystem.
sentences: Code in the iOS 27.3 beta suggests that Apple could add support for chatbots to its smart home hub.
There’s a flag listed for a “Conversational Apps” category.
While there are no details about what apps would fall under that heading, it seems reasonable that AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude could be added to HomeView.

According to pdfu on X, that new beta also adds support for bidirectional audio routing and session management, but says it’s “still not fully wired up.”
Apple has also added anti-spoofing protection that will require a user to authenticate themselves with an iPhone after three failed attempts.
It will also have a lockout system with increasingly longer wait times, starting at one hour for the second lockout, and climbing to eight for the fourth.
Neither feature has been officially announced by Apple, and there’s no word on when they might become available.
